Part (a): dy/dx at (1,−1) = 6(1)(1) = 6. For x<0, y≠0: y²>0 and x<0 so dy/dx<0; all slope segments in the left half-plane (off the x-axis) have negative slope.

Part (b): dy/y² = 6x dx → −1/y = 3x² + C. At (0,−1/2): −1/(−1/2) = 2 = C. So −1/y = 3x²+2, y = −1/(3x²+2).

Part (c): The claim is incorrect. y=0 satisfies dy/dx = 0 = 6x(0)² identically, so it is a solution; it was lost when dividing by y² during separation (a singular/constant solution). Domain of the particular solution: all real x, since 3x²+2 > 0 always.

answers.final_answer: dy/dx = 6 at (1,-1); dy/dx < 0 for all x<0, y≠0, so slope-field segments in the left half-plane (off the x-axis) have negative slope.
